subject: Temporary on-call coverage & freeze-exception request — SRE team
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 2 Apr 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Temporary on-call coverage & freeze-exception request — SRE team

Hi team,

Short version: Rohan Mehta is transitioning to the Eng Manager role effective 4/9 (promotion pending), which leaves a 10-week on-call gap for the Core SRE rotation during a high-launch window. People team informed me we’re still under the hiring freeze, so I’m requesting a temporary freeze-exception to either (A) engage a contracted on-call engineer through AcmeOps for up to 12 weeks, or (B) approve a +1 temporary headcount (fixed-term) to be backfilled against our FY26 cushion.

Why this is urgent:
- We have 3 P1 incidents in the last 30 days and the SLO for error-free deploys is at risk during the rollout scheduled for late April.
- Current on-call bandwidth after Rohan’s move drops 30% in effective paging coverage across nights/weekends.
- Shipping the runtime change without increased on-call coverage increases our incident MTTx risk and could breach enterprise SLAs for two customers (attachments show incident impact).

Options I’d like leadership/People to consider (ranked):
1) Approve temporary contractor (AcmeOps) — fastest (2 week onboarding), estimated cost: ~$75k for 12 weeks (attachment: oncall-coverage-options.xlsx).
2) Approve a fixed-term backfill headcount (12 weeks) and recruit internally — slower (3–5 weeks) but keeps work in-house and supports knowledge transfer.
3) Approve limited overtime/on-call stipend + shift of rotation (internal) — lowest cost but still leaves coverage gaps during peak launch days.

Ask: Laura/Neha — can People approve a freeze exception for option 1 or 2 for up to 12 weeks, and provide an expedited background/KBA path? Vivek/Rishi — can you confirm budget ownership (team commit) if we pursue option 1?

I’ve attached the req draft and a short coverage plan. Happy to stand up a 20-min call this afternoon to walk through tradeoffs.

Thanks,
Grace
Grace O’Connor
Senior Manager, Core Infrastructure
Redwood Inference

Attachments: REQ-4723-oncall-jd.pdf, oncall-coverage-options.xlsx

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 2 Apr 2026 10:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Temporary on-call coverage & freeze-exception request — SRE team

Thanks for the clear summary, Grace.

Neha — high-level: People will consider short-term freeze exceptions for operational risk cases where there is clear customer/SLA exposure. Please provide the minimum approval path and required justification docs.

Grace/Vivek — please send the following by EOD:
- Brief impact statement (1 page) that ties the gap to customer SLA risk and recent incidents.
- Cost delta: contractor vs fixed-term (total $ and approver).
- Onboarding checklist and KBA transfer plan for the contractor.

If we have that, I can fast-track to the Exec HR committee meeting tomorrow. One caution: we need to include a sunset clause (no open-ended hires).

Laura
Laura Bennett
VP, People Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Temporary on-call coverage & freeze-exception request — SRE team

Adding the operational context Grace called out. A few data points to support the request:
- Last 30 days: 3 P1s, total downtime ~85 minutes; two incidents tied to the runtime rollout we’re planning for 4/24.
- Team current headcount (post-transition): 6 full-time SRE ICs + 1 on-call manager; expected effective rotation = 1.7 FTE equivalent for the nights/weekends window.
- Impact to product: potential for delayed incident response and extended customer-facing outages during rollout; both are trigger events for SLA credit discussions.

My preferred mitigation is Option 1 (contractor via AcmeOps) for speed. I commit team budget for the contractor under the Core Infrastructure runbook line (I’ll absorb into Q2 ops spend). If People approves, I’ll sign off on scope, onboarding, and immediately begin contracting.

Grace — sending you the RD for the req and I’ve looped in Sara at AcmeOps for a statement of work.

-Vivek

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 3 Apr 2026 09:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Temporary on-call coverage & freeze-exception request — SRE team

Hi — I reviewed the materials you sent. Quick notes: 
- This meets the operational exception criteria; we can approve a timeboxed contractor engagement up to 12 weeks with a sunset clause and a short retro.
- Required: signed SOW, verification of contractor security screening (AcmeOps provides SOC2 report; request their redacted background-check process), and a KBA/oncall runbook handed off to a named internal owner within 5 business days of onboard.
- Please include RACI for escalations (who pagers first/second) and an assurance that the contractor will not have standing access to production secrets beyond ephemeral keys rotated daily.

Next steps: Grace/Vivek, send the SOW and proposed RACI. Laura — if you’re good with the timeline I’ll mark this approved conditionally and present to Exec HR with the SOW and cost estimate.

Neha Kapoor
Head of Talent Operations (interim)
